gloss: to draw a line; to clearly distinguish

definitions.gloss: to draw a clear line between; to distinguish oneself from; to set oneself apart
definitions.explanation: An idiomatic expression meaning to establish a clear distinction or boundary between two things, or to stand clearly apart from others. Often used to describe how something or someone is distinctly different from comparable things.

examples.japanese: この{作品|さくひん}は{他|ほか}とは{一線|いっせん}を{画|かく}している。
examples.english: This work stands apart from the rest.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}と{私生活|しせいかつ}の{間|あいだ}に{一線|いっせん}を{画|かく}すべきだ。
examples.english: You should draw a clear line between work and private life.

examples.japanese: その{会社|かいしゃ}は{品質|ひんしつ}において{競合他社|きょうごうたしゃ}と{一線|いっせん}を{画|かく}している。
examples.english: That company clearly distinguishes itself from its competitors in quality.

notes:
USAGE:
A formal expression commonly used in written language and news commentary. The pattern is AとBの{間|あいだ}に{一線|いっせん}を{画|かく}す (to draw a line between A and B) or Aと{一線|いっせん}を{画|かく}す (to distinguish from A). The verb {画|かく}す is a literary form of {画|えが}く meaning to draw or demarcate.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {他|ほか}と{一線|いっせん}を{画|かく}す (to stand apart from others)
- {明確|めいかく}に{一線|いっせん}を{画|かく}す (to draw a clear line)
- {一線|いっせん}を{画|かく}した{存在|そんざい} (a distinct presence)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {区別|くべつ}する: to distinguish, to differentiate — more everyday and neutral
- {際立|きわだ}つ: to stand out, to be conspicuous — focuses on being noticeable
